analysis:
The only changed file is docs/architecture/inference.md, with head lines 1742-1868 added: a new "Native Flint" section describing a model_type `flint` adapter (FlintModel, CBv2 prefill without a vocabulary projection for evaluation-only chunks, and a strict loader that rejects missing, extra or duplicate tensors and conflicting aliases). The supplied units are the BASE text for lines 1-821 of the file. They do not contain the new head lines, so I could not cite or inspect the added text directly. The patch excerpt is truncated.

This is a documentation-only change. It touches no code, endpoints, keys, attestation, the coordinator-to-provider WebSocket contract, or prefix-cache storage, so I found no regression against T-041 or the other threats. The patch is described as adding a native model adapter. The documented loader strictness (rejecting extra or missing tensors) is consistent with a fail-closed posture toward T-012 and T-027 (weight substitution).

The adapter's code is not supplied. Open questions for the next pass: whether the Flint adapter is advertised or served by default; whether the model passes the same weight-hash and verification gating; and whether its CBv2 prefix-cache integration, if any, preserves the cacheSalt scoping and HMAC lookup posture in T-041.

The truncated patch excerpt and the missing source for the new adapter limit coverage, so I set needs_deeper_review=true for uncertainty about the code that implements the documented behavior. No finding qualifies on the supplied evidence.
